articles.body: An Olympic silver, three World Championship medals, including a gold, three Commonwealth Games golds and a bronze might seem enough for any athlete. Not for Mirabai Chanu. The missing piece was an Asian Games medal, a dream she had chased since 2013. That wait ended in Nagoya, where the 32-year-old finally clinched silver. Mirabai spoke to Manuja Veerappa & Sabi Hussain about facing her fears and the next Olympic challengeConsidering you missed out on a medal in the previous Games because of an injury, did that weigh on your mind?Of course, I thought about it. Not just here. Even while training, I could never forget that moment. It still hurts a lot. Until now, the Asian Games had been somewhat jinxed for me. I kept thinking about what happened to me in the run-up or during the Games. What was I missing? But this is part of an athlete’s life. We need to face it. If we don’t face it, we won’t get what we want.How different were these Games compared to the previous ones?This time, I didn’t think too much about what I wanted to do or what I didn’t. I came in with a lot of confidence. I knew my training was going well, so I decided I had to return to India with a medal.Having finally won a medal, will this be your last Asian Games?I competed as if this was my last Asian Games. The next one in Doha is four years away, and four years is a very long time in any athlete’s life. I don’t know what life will hold for me by then. For now, I have no plans for Doha. I felt Aichi-Nagoya was perhaps my best — and maybe my only — chance to get on the podium and win the Asian Games medal that was missing from my cabinet. It was a dream to stand on the podium at the Asian Games, and I have finally achieved it. It wouldn’t be an overstatement to say that this medal is no less than an Olympic medal for me because I waited years for it. It has given me immense joy and happiness.What was the focus during your training?We didn’t change much in training. The focus was on staying injury-free and maintaining my fitness. I did a lot of strength training in preparation for this event. We focused more on perfecting my snatch because that was going to be the key.You’ve stayed away from the phone and social media for a while.After the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, my only focus was on an Asian Games medal, and I didn’t want any distractions. I stayed away from my mobile phone and social media. My coach, Vijay Sharma sir, would occasionally make me speak to my family in Manipur. They were the only people I stayed in touch with. Even on days when my training didn’t go well, or I was feeling low, I didn’t speak to my family because that would worry them. It was like I had locked myself in a bubble.Often, women shy away from talking about changes in their bodies, especially during menstrual cycles. But you’ve been open about how being on the third day of your cycle affected you in the Paris Olympics. How important is it to talk to coaches about it?As women, we go through a lot. Periods can be tough, both mentally and physically. So, it is even more important to accept it and be professional and open with your coaches. I know a lot of girls, especially those from rural backgrounds, shy away from talking to male coaches about it. That shouldn’t be the case because then you are the loser. I had my period during the competition in Nagoya, and I discussed it with my coach. As weightlifters, apart from cramps, we have to deal with a tired body and a loose back. Only when we are open about it can coaches decide on load management. I want to tell all female athletes, whether young or old, to speak to their coaches and support staff about what they are going through.What does your success mean for people back home in Manipur?It means a lot, and I’m very happy that over the years, athletes from Manipur have come into focus. I’m glad that I have played a small part in that. It has helped change people’s mindset because, in rural areas, there is hardly any focus on girls, and they are often left out of sports. Girls are game-changers, and parents need to realise that. At the heart of all our success is the support we receive from our families, and every girl who steps into a sporting arena deserves that.Your thoughts on the 2028 LA Olympics…There is no time to rest on my laurels. For me, the road to the LA Games starts now. The ultimate target is to win a medal there. I will be visiting my hometown in Manipur for a while because I haven’t been home in a long time. Then training resumes. In Dec, we will have our first Olympic qualifier. I want to qualify early so that I have enough time to prepare properly. Also, there is no 49 kg weight category at the Olympics anymore. So, I will be competing in the 53 kg category. That’s a fresh challenge for me, moving up to a higher weight category. I will have to put on some weight and make necessary adjustments.

articles.title: Panchang Today, September 27, 2026: Krishan Paksh 1 (Pratipada(Ekam)), U.Bhadrapada, Shubh Muhurat, Rahu Kaal and More
articles.summary: Panchang Today is your steady, everyday compass, built on the Hindu calendar’s time tested wisdom.
articles.body: Panchang Today is your steady, everyday compass, built on the Hindu calendar’s time tested wisdom. It helps you plan with precision, not just by the clock, but by the Moon’s mood, the Nakshatra’s temperament, and the day’s spiritual weather. Some days ask for speed, others ask for softness. Today leans inward, like a river turning quiet after rain. If you stay alert, you can make mindful choices in work, relationships, travel, and prayer, while staying connected to your cultural roots. Below are the important Panchang details for September 27, 2026 for India: Date & Day Details September 27, 2026 falls on a Sunday, a Surya ruled day that nudges you to restore order, self respect, and routine. Yet the lunar side tells a different story, quieter and more reflective. The Tithi is Krishan Paksh 1 (Pratipada(Ekam)), ending at 20:58:47, after which Krishan Paksh 2 (Dvitiya) begins. Pratipada is the first step after the full Moon, when the mind starts withdrawing from noise and turning towards what’s essential. Think of it as the day after a big family function.The house is the same, but you begin putting things back in place. This Tithi supports resetting habits, cleaning up pending matters, and taking a fresh but gentle start. Avoid forcing big, dramatic decisions. Start, yes. Push, no.The Nakshatra is U.Bhadrapada, ending at 11:08:05, and then it moves into Revati. U.Bhadrapada is traditionally linked with depth, stillness, and inner transformation. It asks for sincerity. No half hearted promises. Its presiding energy encourages spiritual study, charitable intention, and mature conversations where you speak less but mean more. Once Revati arrives after 11:08:05, the tone becomes softer and more compassionate. Revati is associated with safe passage, nourishment, and guidance. Good for travel planning, completing work, mentoring someone, or simply taking care of family needs without complaint. A useful shift, if you use the morning for serious focus and the later part for gentle completion.The Moon sign is Pisces 13.37, and it stays in Pisces today. The Moon transitions at 28/09/2026 10:16:17 into Aries, so for September 27 you remain under Pisces influence. Pisces Moon days can feel like a monsoon cloud hanging low, full of feeling. People may be sensitive. Words land deeper than you expect. This is good for creative work, prayer, music, and forgiving old mistakes. It’s also a day to be careful with confusion, misplaced trust, and impulsive generosity. Keep your kindness, but keep your boundaries too.Yoga is Vriddhi till 11:17:04, then Dhruva begins. Vriddhi carries a growth theme, it multiplies what you already have. If you start the day with discipline, results grow. If you start with laziness, distractions grow too. Dhruva later brings steadiness and staying power, helpful for tasks that need consistency, like studies, paperwork, or long pending repairs. Karan is Balava till 09:42:13, then Kaulava till 20:58:47. These Karans support practical work, coordination, and orderly progress. In simple terms, the day rewards calm effort. Keep your pace steady and your mind clean.Auspicious Timings (Shubh Muhurat) Auspicious timings aren’t just lucky slots. They’re like openings in the sky, when the mind and atmosphere cooperate. Use them wisely, even for small things like sending an important email,paying a bill, or starting your study session.Brahma Muhurta runs from 2026-09-27 04:12:27 to 2026-09-27 05:00:27. This is the purest, quietest stretch, when thoughts settle easily. If you’ve been feeling restless, wake up for this and sit with a simple mantra or breath practice. Even 15 minutes of sincere stillness can change your entire Sunday.Pratah Sandhya is from 2026-09-27 04:36:27 to 2026-09-27 05:48:27, a gentle devotional bridge into the day. Good for Surya arghya, reading a few shlokas, or simply planning your tasks without the phone. Amrit Kalam comes from 2026-09-27 06:24:40 to 2026-09-27 07:59:00, a sweet window for starting something that you want to protect and grow, like a health habit, a savings plan, or a calm conversation at home.Sarvartha Siddhi Yoga is available from 2026-09-27 05:48:27 to 2026-09-27 11:07:40. This is a strong supportive period for “things that must work out”, like submitting forms, beginning a serious revision schedule, or arranging a meeting where you need clarity. Abhijit Muhurta is from 2026-09-27 11:24:55 to 2026-09-27 12:12:59. It’s a classic choice for important starts, signing off on plans, or making a key request.Vijay Muhurta, from 2026-09-27 13:49:07 to 2026-09-27 14:37:11, supports victory through effort. Ideal for interviews, competitive exam practice, or a negotiation where you must stay firm but polite.As evening arrives, Godhuli Muhurta runs from 2026-09-27 17:49:18 to 2026-09-27 18:13:18, and Sayahana Sandhya from 2026-09-27 17:49:18 to 2026-09-27 19:01:18. These are beautiful for diya lighting, family prayer, and resetting your mood after a long day.Choghadiya also gives a clean map. In the day, Laabh @ 08:48 supports gains and practical progress, Amrit @ 10:18 supports harmony and success, and Shubh @ 13:18 supports auspicious beginnings. At night, Shubh @ 17:49 and Amrit @ 19:19 are ideal for prayer and family time, while Laabh @ 25:18 and Shubh @ 28:18 suit steady work for those who study or work late.Inauspicious Timings Every day has a few rough patches. These aren’t meant to scare you. They simply remind you to avoid risky beginnings and keep the mind steady.Rahu Kaal today is from 16:19 to 17:49. Rahu Kaal is a shadowy period where confusion, haste, and wrong judgement increase. Avoid launching new ventures, making big financial decisions, signing contracts, or booking high value purchases then. Keep your wallet closed today during this slot, and don’t argue just to prove a point. If you must work, do routine tasks. Chant the Rahu mantra “Om Raam Rahave Namaha” a few times, or sit quietly with slow breathing. Meditation, japa, and simple cleaning work very well in Rahu Kaal.Yamaganda runs from 2026-09-27 11:48:52 to 2026-09-27 13:18:58. This period is traditionally avoided for new starts, especially related to travel or commitments. Use it for continuing existing work, reviewing documents, or finishing household chores you’ve been postponing.Gulkai Kaal is from 2026-09-27 14:49:05 to 2026-09-27 16:19:11. Gulika time can bring delays or minor obstacles. Don’t panic if something moves slowly. Avoid buying gadgets, starting repairs, or making a big promise that you may not keep.Dur Muhurtam appears twice, from 2026-09-27 06:36:31 to 2026-09-27 07:24:31, and again from 2026-09-27 16:13:19 to 2026-09-27 17:01:19. Dur Muhurtam is best treated as a caution sign. Postpone confrontational meetings and don’t send harsh messages. If you’re commuting, be patient. Small distractions cause bigger trouble in these windows.Varjyam runs from 2026-09-27 22:45:30 to 2026-09-28 00:17:57. Varjyam is a “don’t begin” time, especially for important talks, travel starts, or commitments. If you can, keep the late eveningsimple and restful.You also have Baana (Mrityu) from 2026-09-27 13:20:27 to 2026-09-28 05:48:51, and Panchaka from 2026-09-27 05:48:27 to 2026-09-28 05:48:51. On such stretches, tradition advises extra care with avoidable risks. Don’t rush into heavy purchases or unnecessary adventures. Take the safer road.Aadal Yoga is noted from 2026-09-27 11:08:40 to 2026-09-27 13:19:40, with detailed entries in the same range. Treat it as a period where results can feel scattered if you act impulsively. Choghadiya warns too, Udveg @ 05:47, Kaal @ 11:48, Rog @ 14:48, and Udveg @ 16:19. At night, Rog @ 22:18, Kaal @ 23:48, and Udveg @ 26:48 are better for rest than for major decisions. Best use today is simple, steady work, and calm speech.Rahu Kaal Timings Across India Rahu Kaal changes from place to place across India because it is calculated from local sunrise, and sunrise differs by longitude even on the same date. So the Rahu Kaal you follow should match your location’s sunrise based Panchang. The table below shows Rahu Kaal timings for major Indian cities, to help you quickly check the right window for where you are.City Rahu Kaal Mumbai 17:00 - 18:30Delhi (NCR) 16:42 - 18:12Bengaluru 16:41 - 18:12Hyderabad 16:37 - 18:08Chennai 16:30 - 18:01Ahmedabad 17:00 - 18:31Pune 16:56 - 18:26Kolkata 15:57 - 17:28Jaipur 16:47 - 18:17Kochi16:47 - 18:17Lucknow 16:27 - 17:57Indore 16:47 - 18:18Guwahati 15:44 - 17:14Chandigarh 16:43 - 18:13Surat 17:00 - 18:30Visakhapatnam 16:18 - 17:49Nagpur 16:35 - 18:05Coimbatore 16:44 - 18:14Varanasi 16:19 - 17:49Bhubaneswar 16:08 - 17:38Sunrise, Sunset, Moonrise & MoonsetSunrise is at 05:47:46 and sunset is at 17:49:28. That arc of the Sun, especially on a Sunday, is a reminder to carry dignity into ordinary tasks. Even making tea, paying bills, or cleaning your workspace can be a form of worship if done with attention. If the morning feels heavy, step outside for a minute after sunrise. Let the light hit your face, and let your thoughts line up.Moonrise is at 06:01:18 PM, and moonset is at 07:14:18 AM, Sep 28. With the Moon in Pisces, the evening can feel emotional, sometimes dreamy. You may remember old conversations, old faces, old songs. Nothing wrong in that. Just don’t let nostalgia pull you into worry. Moonrise is a good time for a simple prayer, a soft walk after dinner, or journaling. Moonset next morning suggests that late night overthinking won’t help. Sleep is also spiritual medicine. The day’s message is clear, work with the daylight, and let the night wash the mind clean.Vrat/Festival Information & Recommendations Pratipada Shraddha is observed today, set in the context of Ashvina, Pitru Paksha. This is a day to remember one’s ancestors with sincerity and quiet respect. In many Indian homes, Shraddha is not just ritual. It’s a way of saying, “We haven’t forgotten you.” It carries gratitude for the lineage that brought us here, along with a gentle reminder that life is temporary, and relationships deserve care while people are still around.Since the Hindu month is Bhadrapada (amanta) and Ashvina (purnimanta), the Pitru Paksha reference aligns with the purnimanta month, Ashvina. The emotional tone fits the Moon too, Pisces doesn’t rush these matters. It asks you to feel, to pray, and to soften.How should you hold the day? Keep it simple and sattvic in spirit. If you follow family tradition, do your Shraddha related practices with cleanliness, patience, and respect for elders. If you don’t, you can still honour the intention. Offer water with a quiet prayer, feed someone in need if possible, or set aside a small donation in memory of your ancestors. Speak to your parents or grandparents with extra warmth today. You never know what comfort a single call can bring.On the relationships front, avoid digging up old arguments. Pisces Moon and Pratipada can make people sensitive. Choose gentle words, especially at home. At work, use the morning’s supportive windows for planning and prioritising, and keep the afternoon free of risky decisions, since the inauspicious periods cluster there. If you must meet someone, keep the agenda tight. Don’t promise what you can’t deliver.Spiritually, today responds well to quiet discipline. A short Surya prayer after 05:47:46, a focused task list, and a calm lamp lighting around the evening Sandhya can bring a surprising sense of balance.Actionable advice: finish one pending household task, make one respectful call to an elder, and avoid major purchases during 16:19 to 17:49. Then end the night with five minutes of chanting “Om Raam Rahave Namaha” and sleep on time.Get the latest astrology news and horoscope updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.body: Candace Owens has renewed her public allegations against Turning Point USA (TPUSA) over the circumstances surrounding Charlie Kirk’s assassination, putting fresh attention on the organisation’s role in planning the event at Utah Valley University. Owens has pointed to what she describes as inconsistencies in accounts of how the event was arranged and responses to an independent review. However, the claims remain unverified, TPUSA has not publicly responded to the latest allegations, and authorities have arrested Tyler Robinson in connection with Kirk’s killing.Candace Owens makes fresh TPUSA allegationsOwens shared several posts on X after highlighting alleged details from a review of the September 10, 2025 event. One claim questioned whether the local TPUSA chapter had actually initiated the event or whether the organisation’s headquarters had contacted the chapter and specified the location and timing.Owens accused TPUSA of misleading her and the public about the planning process. She wrote, “They gaslit me for a year when I instantly said there was something weird about how quickly this event came together. They represented to the public that the chapter requested it. No. Headquarters requested it and were being vague to the Chapter Leader about it.”She later described the alleged information as significant, writing, “This is the most damning document we have seen since. It confirms what I suspected all along. Everything about the planning was unnatural and it came straight from TPUSA Headquarters.”Owens also expressed her emotions over the dispute, saying, “I am oscillating between the emotions of anger for the lies and gaslighting I’ve been made to endure over the last year, and the relief that comes from being proven correct about what took place. Mostly, I am devastated for Charlie that the organization that he gave his everything to, so callously and unflinchingly partook in a ruthless year long campaign of deflection and obfuscating.”Charlie Kirk assassination claims remain unconfirmedAnother issue raised online involved whether TPUSA representatives responded to investigators conducting the independent review. Owens highlighted a post claiming that reviewers could not obtain a response from a TPUSA-affiliated person despite repeated attempts.She added, “CEO and Chairman Erika Kirk approves this message.”However, an opposing post on X offered a narrower interpretation, claiming that the report referred specifically to Dan Flood and Maycee Crofts, while Brian Harpole was identified as being with Integrity Solutions rather than TPUSA. The post also said the head of UVU’s TPUSA chapter had not responded.These competing claims underline the need for caution. There is currently no confirmation that TPUSA officials were involved in Kirk’s killing. Tyler Robinson has been arrested and faces trial in the case.Owens also suggested that more legal action could follow, while an X account claimed Erika Kirk’s legal team may sue Owens. articles.title: 2 more Naga men killed as ethnic violence flares up in Manipur again
articles.summary: Two Mao Naga men were shot dead by unidentified gunmen at Kalenjang village in Manipur's Senapati district Saturday afternoon, with two others wounded, in
articles.body: Two Mao Naga men were shot dead by unidentified gunmen at Kalenjang village in Manipur's Senapati district Saturday afternoon, with two others wounded, in the latest escalation in a Naga-Kuki conflict that has claimed more than 40 lives since Feb.The shooting took place under Senapati police station around 2.30pm, shortly after CM Yumnam Khemchand Singh left a function about 30km away. It came two days after four Tangkhul Naga men were killed allegedly by Myanmar-based Kuki National Army-Burma (B) at Pilong village near the international border in Kamjong district.The Kalenjang and Pilong killings are part of a series of Naga-Kuki clashes that began in Feb, shortly after Singh's govt took charge. At least 21 people - 11 Nagas and 10 Kukis, including a pregnant woman - have been killed since Aug 27. The toll is separate from the Meitei-Kuki conflict, which has killed over 300.Both the communities have accused militant groups from the other side of the attacks. Police have said several such allegations are under investigation and have not been independently verified.The killings came as United Naga Council (UNC), the apex body of Naga tribes in Manipur, called off its 131-day economic blockade of NH-2 and NH-37 after a meeting with home ministry and Manipur govt at the BSF Frontier headquarters in Guwahati Saturday. The blockade followed the abduction of six Liangmai Naga civilians in Kangpokpi district.Manipur Congress president Okram Ibobi Singh accused BJP-headed NDA govts in the state and Centre of remaining "silent spectators" to civilian killings. "Govt is behaving as if it is not concerned about the killings of civilians of any community," the former three-time CM said. "We strongly condemn the killings of innocent civilians from Naga, Kuki and Meitei communities," he said, while questioning security along the Myanmar border.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘All SIR rollout decisions unanimous’: EC says agendas for all meetings to be circulated in advance
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Election Commission asserted Saturday that the decisions regarding special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls were taken unanimously
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Election Commission asserted Saturday that the decisions regarding special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls were taken unanimously by chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and election commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.The statement came following the first meeting of the "full" Commission after a report in The Indian Express suggested the CEC disregarded the views of the two ECs on SIR-related calls, which sparked a political row, with the opposition targeting the govt and the CEC."The order for SIR issued on 24.6.2025 for all States/UTs, starting with Bihar, followed by West Bengal and 30 other States/UTs was issued with the unanimous approval of the Commission," the EC said.It also denied the claim that Sandhu and Joshi wrote to the Cabinet secretary to flag concerns over policy matters or IT processes.SIR has been implemented in 20 states and UTs and is under way in 12 others. The poll panel also refuted the claim that Sandhu and Joshi wrote separate letters to the cabinet secretary to flag their concerns about policy matters or processes adopted by EC's IT division over which they no longer had control.The letter was "related to the work of an officer on deputation to EC. The work re-distribution orders issued by the officer concerned were not actually implemented after the orders of the two commissioners and the oversight over the IT division by the DEC was never actually withdrawn," EC said.The report said Sandhu and Joshi had called the move "a clear violation" of the law that governs EC and sought action against senior DEC Maneesh Garg, and linked the commissioners' objections to field officers allegedly being locked out of ECINET making it a "centralised" software directly controlled by EC.The allegations linking the commissioners' objections to SIR and alleged lack of access to field officers to ECINET were seized upon by opposition to point their guns at the CEC. LoP Rahul Gandhi demanded he be imprisoned while opposition appeared set to seek his removal afresh.Saturday's full commission meeting and the statement issued later sought to fix this; it cleared the air point by point, besides conveying the message that the three members had resolved their internal issues.EC decided to concede on a slew of matters raised by the commissioners through internal notes, deciding that the agenda for all meetings shall henceforth be circulated in advance and the minutes issued. Also, annual performance appraisal reports of all officers would be completed by Dec 31 every year. The statement said all directions issued by the commissioners to the officers of the commission will be complied with and foreign trips for officers approved by the full commission.On opposition's claim of disenfranchisement of 13 crore voters in SIR, EC said the final figure of electors will be known only after final publication of the roll in the remaining 12 states of Phase 3.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
